title: U.S. House · California's 32nd District
area: West San Fernando Valley and Santa Monica Mountains communities in Los Angeles, including Sherman Oaks, Encino, Woodland Hills, Tarzana, Studio City, Bel Air, and Malibu. District lines were redrawn for the 2026 election under California Proposition 50.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 election cycle after voters approved Proposition 50 on November 4, 2025, a mid-decade redistricting measure.
Incumbent Democrat Brad Sherman, first elected in 1996, and Republican Larry Thompson, an entertainment industry executive, advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.

summary.text: Brad Sherman is the Democratic incumbent for California's 32nd Congressional District and has served in the U.S. House since 1997. A tax lawyer and certified public accountant, he chaired the California State Board of Equalization before entering Congress. He serves on the Financial Services, Foreign Affairs, and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

background.text: Born in Los Angeles, California, in 1954.
Earned a B.A. from UCLA in 1974 (summa cum laude) and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 1979 (magna cum laude), according to his official resume.
Licensed as an attorney in California and certified by the State Bar as a Tax Law Specialist; also a California certified public accountant (inactive).

Worked in the private sector from 1975 to 1990, including as an instructor in the Harvard Law School International Tax Program and as a staff member of a major CPA firm on audits of large businesses and government entities. His resume says he also helped represent the Government of the Philippines in an effort to seize assets of former President Ferdinand Marcos.
Served on the board of California Common Cause from 1985 to 1989.
Served as a member and chairman of the California State Board of Equalization, the state's elected tax commission, from 1991 to 1995, according to his official resume.

First took office in the U.S. House in 1997, representing California's 24th District until 2003 and the 27th and then 32nd Districts thereafter, per Ballotpedia, which lists his current tenure from 2003.

Serves on the Financial Services Committee and the Foreign Affairs Committee (both since 1997), and on the Science, Space, and Technology Committee (1998-1999, 2003-2007, and 2019 to present). He chaired the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Asia, the Pacific, Central Asia, and Nonproliferation during the 116th Congress and co-chairs the CPA and Accountants Caucus.

priorities.text: States he remains committed to fighting gun violence and to protecting the right to abortion and reproductive healthcare.

positions.summary: Says he has fought to protect the right to abortion and reproductive healthcare, helped pass the Women's Health Protection Act in the House to codify the rights once guaranteed by Roe v. Wade, and introduced legislation to help cover travel expenses for abortion care.
positions.quote: Since Sherman's arrival in Congress, he has fought to protect the right to abortion and reproductive healthcare and has consistently earned 100% ratings from NARAL Pro-Choice America and Planned Parenthood for over a decade.

positions.summary: Says he helped pass the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act into law and continues to push for expanded background checks, safe storage requirements, and a ban on high-capacity magazines and assault weapons.
positions.quote: Congressman Sherman remains committed to fighting the scourge of gun violence that has shattered communities across our country.

positions.summary: Says he has supported the Green New Deal since it was first introduced and introduced a resolution disapproving of the Trump administration's 2025 withdrawal from the Paris Agreement, calling for the U.S. to maintain that partnership.
positions.quote: Sherman has supported the Green New Deal since it was first introduced in the House of Representatives and will continue to do so going forward.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and the House Committee on Foreign Affairs in the 119th Congress (2025-2026). In the 118th Congress (2023-2024), served as Ranking Member of the Financial Services Subcommittee on Capital Markets.

candidates.name: Larry Thompson
candidates.currentRole: Entertainment industry executive; founder of the Larry A. Thompson Organization

summary.text: Larry Thompson is the Republican nominee for California's 32nd Congressional District. Born in Clarksdale, Mississippi, he is a lawyer, talent manager, and film and television producer who has lived in Los Angeles since 1968. He describes himself as a moderate Republican; he also ran for the U.S. House in 2020 and 2024.

background.text: Born in Clarksdale, Mississippi; says he was born, raised, and educated in Mississippi.
Earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Mississippi in 1966 and a J.D. from the University of Mississippi School of Law in 1968.
Served in the U.S. Army Reserve, Adjutant General's Corps, from 1968 to 1974.
Has lived in Los Angeles since 1968 and now lives in Malibu, within the district. He is affiliated with the California Bar Association.

Describes himself as founder and president of the Larry A. Thompson Organization. According to his survey, he managed the careers of more than 250 entertainers and produced 23 television movies, five motion pictures, two television series, and 12 television specials, which received awards including the Christopher Award and nominations for Emmys and a Golden Globe.

Says he was inducted into the Hall of Fame of the National Conference of Personal Managers, received a Lifetime Achievement Award from the Talent Managers Association, and serves on the advisory boards of the Delta Blues Museum, Paulist Productions, and Good News Communications.
Ballotpedia lists him as a candidate for the U.S. House in 2020 (defeated in the primary) and 2024, when Rep. Sherman defeated him in the general election.

priorities.text: Says he will "use all of my abilities to support and rebuild the physical and emotional well being of all the people in District 32 who suffered from the recent fires," and describes himself as seeking to find "Common Ground" across party lines.
priorities.quote: As a moderate Republican, I want all to use Common Sense with Common Civility to find Common Ground to solve our Common Issues.

priorities.text: Lists priorities including making California more affordable, securing the border, helping the homeless, and incentivizing music and film production in the district.

researchNotes: Brad Sherman has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions and priorities here are drawn from his official House issues pages on abortion, guns, and climate. No clear statement mapping to tariffs, tax_wealthy, or israel_aid (beyond general support for the U.S.-Israel alliance without a specific aid statement) was found, so those were omitted. His federal floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Larry Thompson completed the 2025 Candidate Connection survey, which is the basis for his priorities here; his responses did not map cleanly to any single fixed issue-key statement with a clear stance, so no positions entries were added for him. Biography notes: Sherman's Board of Equalization service is given as 1991-1995 per his official resume (Ballotpedia says 1990-1995); his 1996 election date is not stated in a loaded source, so the summary now says he has served since 1997. Thompson's biography relies on his own Candidate Connection survey; no independent profile was found.
